guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2 authorization code flow for user-owned applications. The least-privilege documented scope for reading issue titles through the REST API is read_api, which grants read access to the API including all groups and projects. Issue listing is documented at the project and account-scoped endpoints with offset and keyset pagination. Writes stay out of scope by using read_api rather than api. Application registration and token refresh are setup requirements, and the app is user-owned, so distribution to other customer organizations is unresolved.
guide.recommendation: GitLab documents OAuth 2 authorization code flow for user-owned applications. Application registration and token refresh are setup requirements, and the app is user-owned, so distribution to other customer organizations is unresolved.

steps.title: Register a user-owned GitLab OAuth application with read_api scope
steps.detail: In the connected person's GitLab account, open Access > Applications, enter a Name and Redirect URI, select the read_api scope only, and save. GitLab then shows the Application ID and Client Secret. The redirect URI must be the customer integration's HTTPS callback; use the documented path rather than inventing one. Developers do this once for the registered app; this step does not execute any consent or token exchange.
steps.doneWhen: The application appears under Authorized applications with read_api scope and the Application ID and Client Secret are stored securely outside source code.

steps.title: Send the connected person to the consent page and verify the callback
steps.detail: Redirect the customer user to the documented authorization endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, a random state value and scope=read_api. The user approves access in their browser. Verify the callback returns code and the same state value before any token exchange. This is the user consent step; it is not executed by this document.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect returns to the registered callback with a code parameter and the same state value sent in the request.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Send the connected person to the consent page and verify the callback
Done when: The redirect returns to the registered callback with a code parameter and the same state value sent in the request.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: The token endpoint returns access_token, token_type bearer, expires_in and refresh_token.

Read the first page of project issues and capture the Link header
Done when: The response is 200 OK with a JSON array of issues, each with a title field, and a Link header if more pages exist. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

Follow the documented next link for remaining issue titles
Done when: Requests stop when the response Link header no longer contains rel=next, or the response array is empty and no Link is present.

Confirm read-only scope by inspecting the grant, not by writing
Done when: The token info response lists scope read_api and the integration code path has no POST, PUT or DELETE calls to issue endpoints.

Refresh the access token before it expires
Done when: The refresh request returns a new access_token and refresh_token, and a read request with the new token succeeds.

Read the next page of issue titles using the returned Link header URL
Done when: Pagination ends when the response no longer includes a Link rel=next header, the documented end condition for this endpoint. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
